title: AI chatbot companion app Talkie pulled from Apple App Store after investigation
summary: Apple says the Talkie app was removed from the App Store Wednesday due to sexual content, but a report suggests the violations go much further than that and involved minors. AI companion app Talkie removed from the App Store. Image source: Talkie So-called artificial intelligence can't think or reason, so when told to engage in roleplay it usually will without the right safeguards. Some apps that are easily found on the App Store are designed explicitly for roleplay, but tend to be locked behind age gates. As some parents and an investigation from The Bureau of Investigative Journalism discovered, whether these apps are rated 18+ or require age verification, kids often find a way and encounter abusive or sexual content. The report led to an App Store removal according to South China Morning Post , first reported by 9to5Mac , though Apple says it did so due to sexual content and not abuse and use by minors. title: AirFly Drive review: excellent wireless CarPlay for one driver, not two
summary: Twelve South has surpassed many previous wireless CarPlay adapters with its AirFly Drive, and also beaten them on price, but it can get fiddly when more than one person uses it. Don't keep moving this between two cars because it's so small, you will lose it somewhere. Your car may already support wireless CarPlay, in which case the odds are you know it because you'll have already been prompted to turn it on. If you use a wired connection, though, AirFly Drive is a very tempting adapter. Where you ordinarily plug your cable in, you instead plug the AirFly Drive and leave it there. Then once it has been paired with your iPhone , everything works exactly as if it is the phone that is wired in. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

title: How to keep watching DVDs with VLC as Apple phases out Mac DVD support
summary: Apple has started retiring the technology behind its built-in DVD playback starting in macOS 27 . Here's how you can still watch discs on a Mac with an optical drive and VLC. VLC on Mac For now, the change affects developers, not people watching DVDs on their Macs. Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK, so developers can no longer build apps against it with that SDK. The framework itself remains in macOS 27, and Apple says it won't be removed until a future release. DVD Player also remains available and functional in macOS 27. If you have movies on DVD, you don't have to wait for another macOS update to find a different way to play them . The free VLC app can open a DVD as a disc, giving you access to its movie, menus, chapters, audio tracks, and subtitles. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums
